email.subject: Re: Quantum database migration, from 1 April
email.body:
Dave Quantum said on 1 April, in the E2E Test: Quantum Widget Decision memo you saved: "We're switching from PostgreSQL to QuantumDB for the analytics pipeline. 10x query performance, lower licensing cost."

The key decisions list under your name restates the move and adds a 10x gain on analytical queries and a timeline of Q3 2026.

The analytics pipeline is moving from PostgreSQL to QuantumDB, and the case for it rests on the performance and licensing figures. Dave's words give the move and the rationale, but no date. The Q3 2026 window appears only in the list you wrote, and nothing else in the memo ties it to Dave.

I read that as the move being settled rather than proposed, since Dave put it in the present tense. If that holds, the 10x figure and the lower licensing cost are what the decision stands on, so they are the first things to check before anyone plans around them. My read is that Q3 2026 is a planning date that has not yet been confirmed by Dave, so anyone scheduling the cutover should treat it as provisional until he says otherwise. It also suggests that any work built on PostgreSQL analytics may need a second look, though I can't see from here which work depends on it. If the 10x gain was measured on your own analytical queries, that would also settle how far the figure can be trusted across the pipeline.

Three questions: Does the 10x figure come from a benchmark on your own analytical queries? Is Q3 2026 Dave's date, or the one the list carries? Does the lower licensing cost have a number yet?
